company_name: Franklin Templeton, Inc. (formerly Franklin Resources, Inc.)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash-flow statement, 'Stock-based compensation' add-back $197.2M (FY2025 $214.8M, FY2024 $246.1M). No separately disclosed equity-award tax-withholding line and no company-published combined figure, so the cash-flow add-back is used as-is; shares withheld for taxes sit inside 'Repurchase of common stock'.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T21:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 21.11-36.79
inputs.wacc_rationale: UNCHANGED from the prior version: base 10.5% = ~4.2% 10Y UST + ~5.3pp ERP/beta premium for AUM-linked operating leverage to equity and credit markets, plus a 1.0pp regulatory single-point-of-failure premium (Western Asset precedent; criminal proceedings against the former co-CIO still open). USD flows, USD rate. Applied uniformly across the three scenarios (adaptations 7(f)): no per-scenario WACC differences. Evidence that would move it: final resolution of the Western Asset criminal matter with no further firm-level liability would argue for removing the 1.0pp premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Unchanged. Operating leases (ROU assets $760.1M, lease liabilities $977.9M at 2026-09-30) are office leases expensed through occupancy inside operating income under US GAAP, so the lease cost is already inside the EBITDA margin; lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. One treatment (operating cost), no separate lease line.
inputs.nci_treatment: Unchanged in principle: attributable-only. Consolidated Investment Products (CIP assets: cash $1,162.1M, investments $17,167.9M; CIP debt $14,689.7M; redeemable NCI $1,415.9M; nonredeemable NCI $1,355.7M at 2026-09-30) are excluded from the flows -- CIP income sits below operating income and is not in the margin build -- and from net debt. FY2026 net income attributable to Franklin Templeton was $1,075.3M against consolidated $1,502.8M; the $427.5M difference is NCI, almost all CIP. Compensation tied to minority interests in subsidiaries ($59.7M) is inside operating expenses, so that NCI is charged in the flows and not again in the bridge. REFINED this version: Franklin's own direct equity stake in CIPs ($1,346.0M), which is eliminated on consolidation and so absent from the balance-sheet 'Investments' line, is now in the equity bridge, together with deductions for the three claims the 10-K says sit against the cash-and-investments total (see equity_bridge).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, same model as the prior version (2026-09-26). Routed via dcf-methods/SKILL.md: an asset manager's AUM-based fees are a distributable operating cash stream; there are no deposits, insurance liabilities or property book, so the bank, insurer, REIT and LIC rows do not apply. Adaptation 7(d) (excluded income needs its matching asset) is applied for the investment portfolio and 7(f) for risk charged once. THIS IS AN UPDATE. FY0 rolled from FY2025 to FY2026 (10-K for the year ended 2026-09-30). ANCHORS REFRESHED: revenue $9,415.3M (+7.3%, against +3.0% in the prior base and +5.5% in the prior bull); cash $3,227.8M and debt $2,637.8M (company only, ex-CIP), net cash $590.0M; investments $2,807.9M; share count 513.27M; buybacks $533.2M; SBC $197.2M (2.1% of revenue). After the balance sheet date the company drew $300M on its revolver (2026-10-19), which is neutral to net debt, and has two acquisitions pending (Stoneshield, BSP/Encina) that are not modelled. OWNER FCF BASE: last_fcf 270.5 = reported FCF 816.2 (OCF 836.7 less net property additions 20.5) - SBC 197.2 - investment and other income 348.5. This identity figure is a poor guide to earning power in FY2026 for two reasons: consolidated OCF is after $879.7M of net investment purchases by consolidated investment products, which is third-party CLO/fund activity, and net property additions of $20.5M are net of proceeds from selling owned office space (FY2025 $154.5M). The component build does not start from it; it starts from revenue and margins. Model-implied FY2027 base owner FCF is about $1.2bn. FY2026 MARGIN ACTUALS (this build's definition: operating income + depreciation + intangible amortization + impairment, before SBC): operating income 1,175.9 + depreciation and other amortization 109.6 + intangible amortization 198.4 + impairment 33.0 + SBC 197.2 = 1,714.1, or 18.2% of revenue (16.1% after SBC; FY2025 15.5% after SBC). FY2026 carried $100.0M of regulatory settlement and $204.5M of special termination benefits (about $70-76M in each of the two prior years); excluding the settlement and the excess termination cost the margin was about 20.7% before SBC. Management's adjusted operating margin was 28.0% of adjusted revenue, guided to about 30% for FY2027 and a raised target of 35% by fiscal Q4 2029. METHOD CORRECTION -- EBITDA BASIS. The engine deducts SBC from the EBITDA margin driver, so the driver must be a pre-SBC margin. The prior version anchored and ramped the driver on post-SBC history (15.5% FY2025 ex-impairment, 19.7% FY2023, ramp to a 22% mid-cycle) and the engine then deducted SBC a second time: its year-1 owner-EBITDA margin was 14.1% against a 15.5% trough actual on the same basis, in a scenario narrating recovery. The prior post-SBC paths are kept exactly as judged and re-expressed pre-SBC by adding the SBC path. This is worth +3.33/share on the weighted value and is shown as its own bridge line. DRIVERS RE-JUDGED: (1) base year-1 growth 3.0% -> 4.0%: period-end AUM of $1,795.1bn is 3.4% above the FY2026 average of $1,735.4bn, the Q4 revenue run-rate is 3.4% above the full year, long-term net flows were positive in each of the first three quarters, and the fee rate is guided flat. (2) D&A path, all scenarios, from 5-6% of revenue to about 3%: intangible amortization fell from $406.5M to $198.4M as acquired intangibles became fully amortized, taking total D&A to $308.0M (3.3%). D&A is added back in the flows, so this only shrinks the tax shield and lowers value. (3) SBC path re-anchored to the 2.1% actual. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, and what would move each: the post-SBC margin intent of every scenario (rolled one year for base and bull) -- FY2026 landed at 16.1% after SBC against 16.5% in the prior base, i.e. on the path, and the FY2027 step to 18.0% after SBC matches the guided ~2pp adjusted-margin gain plus the roll-off of the settlement; it would move up if FY2027 delivers the ~30% adjusted margin while the gap between adjusted and GAAP operating income (FY2026: $843.5M) narrows, and down on a further impairment or repeat termination charge. Growth beyond year 1 (rolled). Capex path (FY2026's $20.5M is net of property sale proceeds and not a base). Cash tax path 25-27% (FY2026 effective rate on attributable pre-tax income about 27%; cash taxes of $521.4M were inflated by a $156.7M reduction in taxes payable). WACC, terminal growth, terminal cap multiples (12x base, 14x bull, 9x bear) and the 25/50/25 weights. The BEAR scenario is restarted from the FY2026 base and not rolled: its drawdown did not happen in FY2026, so rolling would have dropped the drawdown year from the scenario. TERMINAL: the cap multiple binds in all three scenarios. DATA NOTE: Metrics.csv carries stock_based_comp of 226.6 (FY2025) and 259.9 (FY2024) where the cash-flow statement shows 214.8 and 246.1; this build uses the cash-flow statement.
inputs.share_count_basis: 512.47M shares issued and outstanding at 2026-09-30 (FY2026 10-K balance sheet; includes unvested restricted stock) plus 0.8M dilutive nonparticipating stock units (Note 3) = 513.27M. Matched to the balance-sheet date on purpose: the cover-page count of 511.16M at 2026-10-31 reflects October buybacks paid from cash after the balance sheet, so pairing it with September cash would count that cash twice. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; FY2026 buybacks of $533.2M (including $208.0M bought from Great-West) more than funded the flat count.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR (-11.2%, FY2021 $3.57 to FY2026 $1.97) diverges from revenue (+2.2%) and equity (+2.3%): FY2021 was a peak-market year and FY2023-25 carried the Western Asset outflows, Putnam integration and $648.8M of intangible impairments. EPS 3yr is +4.6% off the FY2023 trough. Neither is extrapolated.
historical_growth.notes: Periods FY2023->FY2026 and FY2021->FY2026. Equity is total stockholders' equity including nonredeemable NCI, as in the prior version; equity attributable to Franklin Templeton fell from $12,077.8M to $11,893.0M in FY2026 on $533.2M of buybacks and $697.6M of dividends. Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - cash-flow-statement SBC - investment and other income, net): FY2023 495.5, FY2024 152.6, FY2025 484.0, FY2026 270.5. The series is dominated by consolidated-investment-product purchases inside OCF (FY2026 -879.7, FY2025 -369.4, FY2024 -520.2) and by the swing in stripped investment income, so its CAGR is not a growth signal. 5yr is null: investment income for FY2021 was not extracted.

base.narrative: FY2026 delivered the recovery the prior base assumed and more on revenue (+7.3%). From here: AUM carries a 3.4% exit-rate lead into FY2027 and long-term net flows stay modestly positive as Western Asset fixed-income outflows fade and alternatives ($304.6bn), ETFs ($84.6bn) and SMAs take share of the mix; the fee rate holds near 41bp as guided. Growth is 4% in FY2027 and tapers to 2%. Margin before SBC rises from 18.2% reported (about 20.7% excluding the $100M settlement and the excess termination charge) to 20.1% in FY2027 and 24% at maturity -- the same post-SBC path as the prior version (18% to 22%), and well short of management's 35% adjusted-margin target, which would be roughly 30% on this definition, because acquisition retention, termination and minority-interest compensation are treated as recurring costs of a serial acquirer.

bull.narrative: Western Asset turns to net inflows, alternatives fundraising holds above the mid-$30bn guide (FY2026: $48.7bn), the ETF platform tracks toward the $200bn target for fiscal 2029, and Franklin Crypto / tokenization becomes a real third leg. Revenue grows 5-6% for three years. Operating leverage and the end of integration charges take the pre-SBC margin to 28.7% (27% after SBC, unchanged from the prior version), close to management's raised target. Exit at 14x.

bear.narrative: Restarted from the FY2026 base. A market drawdown or a second affiliate-level reputational event cuts AUM and fees for two years (-3%, -2%) from a record level; the largely fixed compensation and distribution base cannot flex, so the pre-SBC margin falls from 18.2% to about 15% before a slow rebuild to 19.2% (17% after SBC, unchanged). Passive substitution outruns the alternatives offset, a further legacy-affiliate impairment is likely, and the exit multiple stays at a discounted 9x.

scenario_narratives.base: AUM's exit-rate lead and modestly positive flows give 4% growth in FY2027 tapering to 2%; margin before SBC recovers from 18.2% to 24% as the FY2026 settlement and termination charges roll off, staying well below management's own adjusted targets.
scenario_narratives.bull: Western Asset returns to inflows, alternatives, ETFs and digital assets compound ahead of plan, and operating leverage carries the pre-SBC margin to about 29%, near management's 35% adjusted target; 14x exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: A drawdown or second affiliate shock shrinks revenue for two years from a record AUM base, the fixed cost base compresses margin to about 15% before SBC, a further impairment follows, and the stock exits at 9x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25. Bear stays at 25% (above the 15% default): single-affiliate concentration risk is demonstrated (Western Asset), the criminal proceedings against its former co-CIO are unresolved, and revenue now sits on record AUM after a strong market, which makes a mechanical fee drawdown more likely, not less. Base 50%: FY2026 tracked the base margin path. Bull held at 25% (below the 35% default) because it needs flows, fundraising and margin targets to land together. No going-concern risk: net cash, covenant headroom, facility extended. Would move: bull up if FY2027 shows positive long-term net flows for the full year with the ~30% adjusted margin delivered.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Franklin Templeton is valued as an operating company on an owner-FCF DCF: AUM-based fees become distributable cash with no deposit funding or post-interest flow to complicate it. The flows are attributable-only operating flows; 'Investment and other income, net' is stripped and the assets that earn it go into the equity bridge at carrying value -- the company's investments plus its own equity stake in consolidated investment products, less the partnership, repo-financing and deferred-compensation claims against them. Third-party CIP assets and debt are excluded on both sides. This version rolls the base year to FY2026, in which revenue beat the prior base by about 4% and margin tracked it. It also corrects a basis error: the prior version fed post-SBC margins into a driver from which the engine deducts SBC, charging SBC twice. The scenario margin judgments themselves are unchanged. The terminal cap multiple binds in every scenario, so value is driven by the margin path and the 9x/12x/14x exit, not by terminal growth.
key_risks_to_valuation: A second reputational or redemption shock at an affiliate, echoing Western Asset; the former co-CIO's criminal proceedings are still open
Revenue sits on record AUM of $1,795bn: a market drawdown cuts fees mechanically against a largely fixed compensation and distribution base

The gap between management's adjusted operating income and GAAP ($843.5M in FY2026: retention, termination, amortization, settlement) keeps recurring -- the base case assumes the settlement and excess termination cost roll off in FY2027
Active-to-passive fee compression eroding the ~41bp fee rate faster than alternatives and SMAs offset it

Further intangible impairments or acquisition spend: up to $375M of Putnam/Great-West contingent payments and up to EUR125M for Apera run through future costs, and pending deals (Stoneshield, BSP/Encina) consume cash not modelled here
Equity bridge precision: the three deductions against investments are the 10-K's 'approximately' figures, and investments are at carrying value, not a liquidation value
